column3: Origami. The triangle is a sheet of paper, and the triangular lattice is literally an origami crease pattern (60-degree grid, as in tessellation folding). Light rakes across the paper, so mountain and valley folds catch it and shade, which needs real 3D-ish shading of facets. The time is folded into the paper: digits as raised pleats or creases. Minute turn: the sheet visibly unfolds the changed digit flat and refolds the new one along the lattice lines, facets rotating in 3D. Hour: the whole sheet folds itself into a crane (or a frog that jumps), then unfolds back to a flat sheet with the new hour. Apex points left (at the connector); you may use the shape as the paper's corner or tip.

Bookshelf cat. The 32x8 strip is a bookshelf seen from the front: books with coloured spines and varied heights, a few leaning; their arrangement (heights, gaps, colours) carries the time. A cat lives on the shelf: it walks along, sniffs, sits, tail swishing, and is drawn with care, 6+ LEDs. Minute turn: the cat bats a book and it topples into the gap, or the cat pushes books around to rearrange the shelf into the new time. Hour: a whole row of books dominoes down and the cat sits proudly at the end, then a hand restacks them. Playful, warm lamp light, wood shelf.

Broadway Boogie Woogie. Piet Mondrian's last painting, alive: the 20x20 square is a Manhattan grid of yellow streets, with little red, blue and grey blocks travelling along them like taxis and pedestrians, pulsing to boogie-woogie rhythm. The blocks gather at intersections and park into the numerals (De Stijl letterforms: only horizontals, verticals and primary colours). Minute turn: traffic disperses from the changed digit and flows into the new one. Hour: a big Mondrian rectangle composition sweeps in (black lines, primary planes), then dissolves back into the traffic. Bold, graphic, rhythmic.

Light cycles. The 61-degree parallelogram leans forward like speed itself. Two Tron light cycles (cyan and orange) race across the dark rhombic grid, and their light walls are the digits: cyan draws the hours, orange the minutes, turning sharply along the lattice's two directions. Grid lines pulse faintly. Minute turn: the cycle whose digit changes derezzes its wall (it shatters into voxels that fly off) and races in a new wall. Hour: both cycles crash head-on in a burst and respawn. Small board (128 LEDs, 52x19 mm): letterforms must be designed for 8 rows on a slant.

Molecules. Three hexagons in a triangle cluster are a chemist's hex grid: skeletal formulas are drawn on exactly this lattice. The time is written as molecules: each digit is a skeletal-formula chain of carbon atoms with zigzag single bonds, double bonds and the odd O (red) or N (blue) atom; the atoms vibrate, and electron clouds shimmer. Minute turn: a reaction mechanism, with curly arrows sweeping, bonds breaking and forming, to turn the old digit-molecule into the new one. Hour: catalysis, an enzyme pocket closes or a flame of combustion, and all bonds reorganise. The seams are the boundaries between three reaction flasks or just three fused rings. Nerdy and beautiful.

Kite. The rhombus of two triangles base to base is a diamond kite flying in a dusk sky, its spars along the board's diagonals and its sail cloth rippling with real wind waves. The digits are painted on the sail, so they ripple with the cloth and catch the light as it flexes. The tail of bows trails off one corner, fluttering. Minute turn: a gust makes the kite loop the loop; it flips to its other side, which carries the new time. Hour: a second kite swoops in for a kite fight, strings cross, and the loser spirals away with the old hour. Dusk palette, warm sail.

Ski slope. The tall slanted parallelogram is a mountain slope seen from above, fresh powder glinting. The digits are ski tracks: a skier (well drawn, poles, scarf) carves each digit down the slope in turns, spraying snow, so the time is literally carved. Pine trees and slalom gates dot the sides. Minute turn: the snow groomer (piste basher) smooths away the changed digit with its blade and tiller, and a skier carves the new one. Hour: an avalanche of powder washes down the whole slope and the hour is re-carved by a whole ski school in a line. Cold whites and blues, a warm sun.

Revolving lanterns. Three hexagonal Chinese palace lanterns (宫灯) hang in a row, red silk and gold frames, tassels below, candles inside. Each is a 走马灯 (trotting-horse lantern): the candle's heat turns an inner paper cylinder, and the silhouettes of galloping horses, riders, cranes or carp run round the inside of the paper. The time is cut into the shadow puppets: the hour in the first lantern, minutes in the other two, as paper-cut (剪纸) numerals carried round on the turning cylinder. Minute turn: the cylinder spins faster and a new cut-out comes round. Hour: the lanterns sway, and fireworks burst behind them. Warm candle flicker, red and gold. The owner is Chinese; make it authentic.

Bowling alley. Three stacked strips are three bowling lanes seen from above, glossy maple wood with arrows and lane oil glints, the seams the gutters. At the far end of the lanes the pins stand, and their racks are arranged into the time (numerals made of pins; the white pins with red necks). Balls roll down with spin and curve. Minute turn: a ball strikes the changed digit's pins, they scatter physically (rotating, sliding), the pinsetter sweeps them away and lowers a new rack in the new digit's shape. Hour: a strike on all lanes at once, confetti on the scoreboard. Physical and satisfying.

Frogger, starring the owner's avatar: a rainbow frog in round blue glasses, pink lips and eyelashes (see the file 71566a08314183249d50a1e5936940a5.jpg in the project root, /Users/bilibili/coding/1602display/). The 32x32 panel of four strips is the classic arcade road-and-river: lanes of cars and trucks below, logs and turtles on the river above, the seams the lane edges. The traffic and logs are cut into the numerals as they scroll, like a moving marquee, so the time is spelled by the world itself. The frog hops up the lanes; at the minute turn it reaches a lily-pad home bay and the traffic changes to spell the new minute. Hour: all five home bays fill, the frog does a victory dance, a snake slithers by. Retro but smooth, not stepped.

Copperplate. Two parallelograms end to end form a long italic band, and the lattice is already slanted at 61 degrees like copperplate script. A pointed dip pen writes the time in flowing cursive: hairline upstrokes, swelling shaded downstrokes as the nib flexes, ink pooling and drying from wet-glossy to matte. Draw the digits as true copperplate numerals (or written-out words if you can make them fit and read). Minute turn: blotting paper rolls over the changed digit, lifting it away, and the nib writes the new one stroke by stroke. Hour: a flourish, a big swash across the band, and a wax seal pressed beside it. Sepia ink, cream paper, a candle's warmth.

Flipbook. Two parallelograms stacked along the slant look like an open flipbook in perspective, its pages fanning. A hand-drawn doodle character lives in the margins: a stick figure, a little dinosaur, or the owner's frog, who runs, jumps, juggles digits and builds the time each minute, animated at flipbook frame rate with paper-flicker. The time is drawn as pencil sketch numerals on the page. Minute turn: a thumb riffles the pages and the animation plays: the character kicks the old digit off the page and draws the new one. Hour: the book flips all the way to a new chapter with a fancy title page. Pencil-grey on paper, one accent colour.

Gothic lancet window. The arc triangle is exactly the shape of a Gothic pointed arch, and its LEDs sit on arcs struck from the two base corners: the very compass geometry medieval masons used for tracery. Make it a stained-glass lancet window: deep ruby, cobalt, gold and emerald glass between dark lead cames, light streaming through, dust motes in the beams. The real sun position drives the light: morning sun from one side, evening from the other, moonlight at night. The time is in the glass: the hour in the window's medallion, the minutes as a row of panes or a figure's halo. Minute turn: a pane's light shifts as a cloud passes and the glass re-colours. Hour: the bells ring and the whole window blazes as the sun breaks through.

Butterfly. Two arc triangles apex to apex are a butterfly's two wings, the apexes meeting at its body. The wing patterns carry the time: the hour on the left wing, the minutes on the right, drawn as eyespots, veins and scale colours (morpho iridescent blue, or monarch orange and black, or a peacock butterfly's eyes). The wings flap slowly, with 3D shading as they tilt, and the scales shimmer with angle-dependent iridescence. Minute turn: the wing pattern morphs, scales ripple and change colour like a living display. Hour: the butterfly takes off (wings beat fast, blur), circles, and lands with a new pattern. The bipolar arc lattice gives natural curved wing veins.

Time-lapse flower. Three arc triangles round a point are a three-petalled flower (trillium) seen from above, with a glowing centre where the apexes meet. The petals' veins follow the boards' arc rings. The flower breathes in time-lapse: petals open in the morning and half-close at night (real time), dew drops glint and roll, and a ladybug (well drawn) walks along the petals. The time is in the petals: one petal for the hour, two for the minutes, as vein patterns, pollen dots or petal colour gradients that read as numbers, or another system that reads clearly. Minute turn: a petal ripples and its pattern regrows. Hour: a bee lands, pollen bursts, and the petals turn a third of a turn.
